To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

student teachers on the course were able to form a cohesive community of practice in their own right, but this community was in tension with the dominant culture of the college and the wider context of FE in England.
the PGCE PCE course is not a community of practice in the sense of a shared identity of literacy teaching in FE.

the PGCE PCE course provides a strong community of practice for the student teachers in terms of the shared understandings that are developed about what it means 'to be' and to 'become' a literacy teacher.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the 'theoretical' and the 'practical' in the development of a professional identity for literacy teachers in the further education sector in England.
the question of how student teachers learn to become members of their new community and how this relates to their experience of HE and the placement setting.
the relationship between the HE component of a teacher training course and the placement experience.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the communities of practice model is a useful one to describe the process of becoming a teacher in the FE context.

student teachers' experience of a community of practice is not a simple process of acculturation but a complex one in which they are required to navigate their way through a number of competing communities.

the communities of practice model is not an adequate way to conceptualise the experience of student literacy teacher in FE settings in the UK, but that it is possible, in the current context, to develop a community of practice within a tutor group that is able to sustain shared values and a shared understanding of what it means to become a literacy teacher in FE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the student teachers were able to create and sustain a community of practice that was based around a shared understanding of literacy teaching in FE.
student teachers are members of a community of practice in which the values and norms of a wider community of practice (that of FE teachers) are not necessarily shared.
the communities of practice model is useful in describing the experience of the PGCE PCE student teachers in the tutor group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
student teachers are able to develop a strong sense of community with their tutors and fellow students in their PGCE PCE course.

there is a need to recognise and acknowledge the existence of competing communities of practice in the context of teacher education in FE colleges and to recognise that the 'community of practice', as it has been described, is a contested and contested space.
the concept of communities of practice can be used to illuminate the experience of post compulsory education student teachers, but only if it is used with caution.
